description: OpenAPI 3.0 path-operation coverage and exhaustive source-artifact disposition evidence.

scenarios.description: A generic OAS 3.0 raw-binary request body is represented for its declared concrete media type without a media-selection requirement.
An exact schema-omitted OAS 3.0 raw-byte operation is fully represented without a media-selection requirement.

A multipart part declaring no `type` (a bare description) has no default concrete type on the 3.0 line, but it remains representable through the family specification's `propertyMedia` configuration point. The governing sentence is: `It is required ... for a multipart part whose resolved declaration is typeless`; therefore the alternative carries the corpus's configuration.propertyMedia requirement instead of being excluded. The request body here is OPTIONAL, so the target itself needs no configuration to remain invocable bodyless.

scenarios.description: String content parses under the YAML 1.2.2 grammar pin, and its plain scalars resolve by the core schema's tag resolution: date-shaped, time-shaped and YAML 1.1 boolean-word scalars match none of the null, bool, int or float patterns, so each is a string. The restriction is the artifact authority's, which limits tags to those allowed by YAML's JSON schema ruleset, so no accepted edition carries a timestamp-tagged node. The string-carried document synthesizes exactly as its JSON spelling does.

scenarios.description: A reference's fragment addresses what looks like a sibling member of a $ref node, and on the 3.0 line there is no such member to address. The Reference Object is defined by JSON Reference, whose section 3 states that any members other than "$ref" in a JSON Reference object SHALL be ignored, so `Alias` has exactly one denotable member and the token `properties` cannot name the declared sibling. Evaluation therefore continues into the referenced value exactly as it does when no sibling is declared, and the emitted value is `Real`'s, not the sibling's. The assertion is the whole scenario: the operation set is identical under either reading, and only the value distinguishes them.

source.content:
openapi: 3.0.4
info: {title: Entry, version: "1"}
servers: [{url: "https://api.example"}]
paths:
  /items:
    post:
      operationId: createItem
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/json:
            schema:
              type: object
              properties:
                pick: {$ref: "./library.yaml#/components/schemas/Alias/properties/name"}
      responses: {"204": {description: ok}}

resources.https://composition.example/library.yaml:
openapi: 3.0.4
info: {title: Library, version: "1"}
components:
  schemas:
    Alias:
      $ref: "#/components/schemas/Real"
      properties:
        name: {type: string, title: sibling}
    Real:
      type: object
      properties:
        name: {type: integer, title: target}

scenarios.description: The retention consequence of OAPI30-SS-31's reading, as a defect, and the twin of OAPI31-SS-34. On the 3.0 line the fragment's next token cannot name an ignored member, so what the pointer runs into is the reference itself: the reference is composed, its target is inside the closure, and a target that is never declared makes the whole source unresolvable. Nothing about the sibling's own shape changes that, which is what separates a reference the closure composes from one a pointer merely walks past.

scenarios.description: A urlencoded property whose resolved schema declares a choice with MORE THAN ONE non-null branch has no single faithful form carriage, so openbindings.openapi-3.0@1 Section 9.2 refuses that alternative before dispatch — and it does so on every accepted edition, including the 3.0-line patches whose own text states no lane-selection rule. Those four editions reach the content path through their own Section 4.1 ("The patch version SHOULD NOT be considered by tooling, making no distinction between 3.0.0 and 3.0.1 for example") together with 3.0.4's Section 4.7.15.1.2 ("Encoding is to be based on contentType alone"), so a part carriage IS resolved here and the two-branch anyOf is caught. A processor that keyed this on the patch component would instead put the property on the RFC6570-style path, which checks only that a coherent serialization method exists, never resolves a part carriage, and would therefore ADMIT the declaration and serve it. Three accountings are pinned because the artifact's requestBody shape decides which applies. toggleWarninglist keeps a JSON sibling, so only its urlencoded alternative is excluded and both the target and the operation's input survive through the other candidate. toggleWarninglistOnly declares urlencoded as its only request media AND marks the body required, so the same defect leaves no invocable form at all and excludes its TARGET, recorded on the target entry alone (openapi.media_schema_mismatch) — the established sole-candidate accounting OAPI31-SS-30 pins. toggleWarninglistOptional is the third cell and the one the corpus actually moved: urlencoded as the ONLY content entry with NO required key. Read at its own artifact bytes, that is the shape MISP/MISP POST /warninglists/toggleEnable has (its requestBody $refs a component declaring application/x-www-form-urlencoded alone and carrying no required), and it was the sole specimen movement of the 2026-08-17 lane ruling. Because the body is optional the operation remains invocable with no body, so its target stays represented and the excluded alternative is the only place the loss is accounted; the published operation consequently advertises NO input at all while the artifact declares a form field, which the assertion on /operations/toggleWarninglistOptional/input pins directly rather than leaving to be inferred from the coverage entries. recordPlace is the unaffected control: an ordinary object property on the same content path.

info.title: Non-collapsing choice in a urlencoded body

scenarios.description: A style-lane declaration whose resolved schema carries a member with no defined expansion is refused at ADMISSION and accounted, not published as represented and refused at invocation. The offending member is an array whose resolved items are object or array, or an object one of whose resolved property schemas is. Every style this lane serves expands a composite value exactly one level — each member becomes a member string — so every value conforming to such a declaration is one the candidate is statically guaranteed to refuse, and the refusal is decided by the declaration alone. The governing text is read per edition. The form row cites [RFC6570] Section 3.2.8 on every accepted edition, and RFC 6570 Section 2.4.2 applies the expansion process "to each member of the composite as if it were listed as a separate variable", whose expansions append member strings. The deepObject row cites no RFC section on any edition: on 3.0.0 through 3.0.3 and 3.1.0 it reads "Provides a simple way of rendering nested objects using form parameters", which governs this case without defining it, and on 3.0.4, 3.1.1 and 3.1.2 it says so outright — "The representation of array or object properties is not defined." No accepted edition supplies a representation, and this specification authors none. listRecords is the mover: its deepObject filter declares a `where` property of type object, so its TARGET is excluded under openapi.parameter_style_expansion_excluded (OAPI30-P-02) — a parameter has no sibling alternative to fall back to, so the unit that owns the defect is the operation. countRecords is the control that matters most: the same style on a bare `{type: object}` declaring NO members at all. Its runtime members may all be scalars, so a declaration-keyed refusal must not reach it and the operation stays represented. listTags is the scalar-list control. upload carries the body half of the same rule: an Encoding Object writing an explicit `style` puts the property on the RFC6570-style lane, its array of objects has no member expansion, and there the smallest owning unit is the ALTERNATIVE — the request media is excluded under openapi.request_media_excluded (OAPI30-P-03) while the target survives, because the body is optional and the operation remains invocable with no body. The published operation consequently advertises no input at all, which the assertion pins directly.

The 3.0 half of the pair OAPI31-SS-37 opens: the same two parameters, the same member bytes, and BOTH operations represented. Every 3.0 edition states of the Schema Object that "type - Value MUST be a string. Multiple types via an array are not supported", so on that line an array-valued `type` is not a union declaration this specification can read, there is nothing to collapse, and neither member resolves to `object`. The pair is what keeps the collapse edition-scoped rather than asserted of every accepted edition: a processor that applied the 3.1 reading to a 3.0 artifact would exclude nullableObjectMember here too, and one that applied the 3.0 reading to a 3.1 artifact would admit it there.

The COVERAGE half of the 3.0 `format: byte` cell. Every accepted 3.0 edition's own Data Types format registry defines `byte` as "base64 encoded characters", so an exact non-JSON, non-form declaration governed by a `type: string`, `format: byte` schema has a defined carriage — the caller's artifact-encoded text, sent as-is — and its alternative is REPRESENTED. Before that lane existed the same declaration fell to an exclusion: application/pdf is outside section 9.2's closed character-data test, so no string-carriage lane applied, and with the byte cell unanswered the alternative had no candidate at all. uploadPlain is the control that shows the lane is keyed on the `byte` DECLARATION and not on the media type: the identical application/pdf declaration carrying a bare `type: string` still has no defined carriage, and because its body is required and that is its only alternative the target itself is excluded under the standing openapi.unresolvable_request_body convention. The same bare-string declaration is what a `format: byte` schema becomes on the 3.1 line, where `format` is an annotation with no content-encoding force and `byte` is absent from the format tables — that line spells an already-encoded string with `contentEncoding` instead.

F-O1-13, the portable statement of the ruled outcome. A boolean-literal Schema Object is legal on the 3.1 line, whose Schema Object IS a JSON Schema 2020-12 schema, and is not a Schema Object at all on the 3.0 line: that line's Schema Object is the Wright Draft 00 subset, where "A JSON schema MUST be an object" (draft-wright-json-schema-00 Section 4.4), each value of `properties` "MUST be an object" (its validation companion Section 5.16), and OAS 3.0.4 Section 4.7.24 says "Property definitions MUST be a Schema Object and not a standard JSON Schema" with `additionalProperties` the only position that line grants a boolean. So the spelling is a DEFECT there — and Section 3's acceptance floor confines a defect to the smallest unit that owns it, which here is the request media alternative carrying the part. That alternative is accounted `invalid` under openapi.invalid_unit, never a whole-source refusal, and not the ordinary media exclusion either: the artifact is upstream-invalid at that position rather than merely uncarriable, which is the distinction the two reason codes keep. The two operations are the two consequences of that one confinement. `upload` declares a healthy application/json sibling, so the invalid alternative costs only itself and the operation stays represented and invocable. `uploadAvatar` declares the same defective alternative as its ONLY one against a required body, so it reaches the standing openapi.media_schema_mismatch target exclusion — the confinement bounds the blast radius at the unit, it does not make every unit survive. The 3.1 half of this cell is not here because it is not a defect at all: `true` is a legal schema that asserts nothing, so it is the type-absent part cell, which carries octets across the canonical Base64 boundary as OAPI31-SS-23 and OAPI31-SS-24 pin.

The 3.0-line twin of OAPI31-SS-23. No accepted 3.0 edition states a default contentType row reaching a part that declares no `type`, and openbindings.openapi-3.0@1 authors none, so that part's content type is the required `propertyMedia` configuration point. The consequence for synthesis is that the alternative is REPRESENTED carrying a configuration requirement, not excluded: what is missing is a settled configuration value, not a carriage the specification lacks. uploadAvatar carries the requirement on its sole alternative and on the target; createNote carries it only on the multipart alternative, because its JSON alternative needs no choice and the target can act through that one; createLabel, whose part declares `type: string`, takes 3.0.4's `text/plain` row read line-uniformly and requires nothing.

info.title: Type-absent form parts on the 3.0 line

scenarios.description: The 3.0 line's half of the same class, and the reason its treatment is not the 3.1 line's. That line's Schema Object is "an extended subset of the JSON Schema Specification Draft Wright-00", and no meta-schema for that draft was ever published -- so a conformant processor has nothing to point at there and reads the edition's own sentences. Two of them decide this scenario. Section 4.7.24.1 lists `required` among the keywords "taken directly from the JSON Schema definition and follow the same specifications", and that definition makes it an array whose elements are unique, so `listContainers` carries an invalid unit exactly as its 3.1 sibling does. And a BOOLEAN `exclusiveMinimum` is this line's own correct spelling -- the draft it extends defines the keyword as a boolean modifier on `minimum` -- so `listBounded` is represented, where the identical declaration on the 3.1 line would be invalid. A processor that decided this line by validating against JSON Schema 2020-12 would refuse what the edition admits; one that decided it by an enumeration missing the uniqueness rule would deliver a document position the edition rejects. Both operations together pin the line's own answer.

A callback operation becomes a targetless Core dependency whose consumed contract takes the request the service sends as input and the expected response as output; its runtime-expression destination never becomes a binding target [OAPI30-S-01].

A request-body Schema Object whose `allOf` branches intersect emptily is a WELL-FORMED upstream declaration that admits no instance, and the JSON-lane position it governs is accounted `represented` with `fullyRepresented: true`. The governing dialect's validity condition for `allOf` is structural only — a non-empty array whose elements are valid schemas — and neither that dialect nor any accepted OAS edition gives satisfiability any role, so nothing about `allOf: [{type: string}, {type: object}]` is upstream-invalid; Core OBI-D-17 says the same from the other side, requiring no proof of satisfiability for a schema to be well-formed. §12.2 admits `invalid` only where the declaration is upstream-invalid, and §3.2 keeps `invalid` and `excluded` apart on exactly that line, so this position is neither: the emitted OBI carries the declaration as written, nothing is projected away, and coverage stays fully represented. The `application/json` lane is selected by media type rather than by the resolved declaration, which is why no admission test gates this position; the intersecting sibling is the control that keeps the scenario about the empty intersection rather than about `allOf`. Where the resolved declaration DOES select carriage — the character-data and raw-octet lanes, a multipart part, a urlencoded property — §9.1's stated no-admissible-candidate rule excludes the alternative instead, which is a different rule with a different status and is not asserted here.

A content-form property or multipart part whose Schema Object `allOf` branches intersect emptily is a WELL-FORMED declaration that admits no instance, and it is an UNREACHABLE defect under Section 3.2's smallest-owner rule: no value can ever reach it, so it destroys neither its media alternative nor its target, both are accounted represented, and the declaration is carried into the synthesized contract as written. This is the same accounting both content-based lanes already apply to a boolean `false` property, of which the empty intersection is the resolved form; it is NOT the accounting for a property with no single faithful carriage (OAPI30-SS-35), where conforming values exist and the lane cannot carry them, nor the style lane's statically-refused member (OAPI30-SS-36), where every conforming value is refused — here there is no conforming value at all, and exclusion would remove a target on a defect nothing reaches. Three requestBody shapes are pinned so the accounting cannot depend on them: a required multipart body whose only alternative carries the property, the same alternative beside an application/json sibling, and an optional urlencoded body. The invoke half — a value supplied for the property refuses before dispatch at that part, Section 5.2's consequence — is pinned by the companion processor scenario on this line. This scenario exists because the two reference engines disagreed here (one excluded the target, one represented it) while agreeing on the boolean false, and the corpus was silent.

Path-template synthesis preserves the 3.0 authority boundary. A repeated expression is upstream-valid and remains represented, with one effective path Parameter supplying every occurrence; an expression with no corresponding effective path Parameter is upstream-invalid and is accounted invalid rather than excluded (OAPI30-S-01, OAPI30-P-02).
A source whose sole addressable operation is upstream-invalid is still accepted and synthesized; the target is accounted invalid rather than being reclassified as a whole-source refusal.

A failure-only Response defect and an impossible 204 body declaration are subordinate coverage loss: both operations remain represented while the exact Response projections are accounted invalid and excluded.
Header-name synthesis confines a non-token optional name to one excluded projection, propagates a non-token required name to its target, and excludes a processor-owned Transfer-Encoding target.
A non-HTTP artifact Server leaves the operation represented and records the server configuration requirement needed to obtain a dispatchable completed target.
Non-token cookie parameters and response Header Object keys are accounted at their smallest projections, with required cookie and response-header forms propagated only to their load-bearing owners.
A default-only Responses Object is valid; the operation and its fallback Response projection remain fully represented.
A required structured-cookie parameter makes the raw-Cookie credential alternative unusable, but the non-colliding OR alternative preserves the target.
A required fixed-destination collision excludes only its credential alternative and preserves a safe OR sibling; the same collision with an optional parameter is not a static exclusion.
TRACE excludes each credential-emitting security alternative, preserves an anonymous sibling when present, and excludes only the target left with no safe alternative.
A coherent case-folded response Header group remains represented, while a mandatory Content-Encoding group with an empty finite-domain intersection is excluded only at its response alternative.
A conflicting case-folded Encoding Header group is excluded at the multipart media alternative while a coherent JSON sibling preserves the required-body target.
An unrepresentable multipart property name is accounted at its media-alternative owner while the target and an unrelated operation remain represented.
A required request Content-Encoding parameter on a target with no surviving request lane excludes only that target; an unrelated operation remains represented.

Every malformed Server Variable form on this edition is invalid at its Server-alternative owner (absent required default, wrong-typed required default); the operation remains represented with the configuration.server recovery requirement.

Empty-enum and out-of-enum-default Server declarations are upstream-valid 3.0 narrowings, so each is excluded only at its Server alternative while both operations remain represented with configuration.server recovery.

A URL expression without a matching Server Variable declaration remains a represented Server alternative and operation; synthesis records configuration.server because an exact consumer substitution can complete it.

Synthesis removes an optional non-token header projection before caller-key uniqueness is computed, so the surviving same-named query parameter remains represented under its unqualified operation-input key.
An artifact-fixed literal filename preserves its multipart alternative, while filename* excludes only its media alternative and leaves a JSON sibling and both operations represented.
A response media range carrying a case-insensitive q parameter is excluded only at that alternative, while a valid sibling and the target remain represented.
OAS 3.0 form-cookie array and object declarations remain represented regardless of required or explode; only an actual multi-value invocation is refused.
A required Request Body target is excluded only when confinement removes every request-content alternative; a valid sibling alternative preserves the target and is represented.
